intro: Backup exports settings, users, mounts, path metas and shares into one JSON file. Restore only adds and updates — it never deletes anything.
encrypt_hint: Encrypted backups use the same field-level AES format as the legacy frontend, so files stay interchangeable in both directions.
secret_warning: An unencrypted backup contains mount credentials and share passwords in plain text. Store it accordingly.
gathered: Collected: settings {settings} · users {users} · mounts {storages} · metas {metas} · shares {shares}
encrypted_hint: The file is encrypted with your password — restore will ask for it.
plaintext_hint: The file is plaintext. Anyone who has it can read your credentials.
gather_failed: Could not read: {names}. Backup aborted so the file is never half-empty.
restore_note: Adds missing items, and updates existing ones when override is on
drop_hint: Drop a backup .json here, or choose a file
override_hint: Off: existing users / mounts / metas / shares are skipped. On: they are overwritten by the file. Settings are always merged and never deleted.
confirm_body: settings {settings} · users {users} · mounts {storages} · metas {metas} · shares {shares}. Mode: {mode}.
mode_override: add missing items and overwrite existing ones
mode_add: add missing items only, skip everything that already exists
aborted: Restore aborted: could not read the current state to reconcile against
self_lockout: Restore refused: this file would demote or disable the account you are logged in as ({name}). Nothing was written.
user_created_disabled: User {name} created disabled with a random password — reset the password before enabling it
log_placeholder: Log lines from the last backup or restore show up here.
err_invalid_json: That file is not valid JSON
err_not_a_backup: That JSON is not an OpenList backup
err_no_sections: The file has no settings / users / mounts / metas / shares section
err_wrong_password: Wrong password (or the file never had one and is encrypted)
err_corrupted: The password is right but the payload is corrupted — is the file truncated?
